title: Removal of the Green System Engine Driven Pump
abstract: Removal of the green system engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox drive pad, including the drive pad cavity inspection that is required whenever a pump is removed for a suspected seal leak.

sections.purpose: This task removes the green system engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox drive pad and records the condition of the drive pad cavity, which is the evidence used to decide whether the shaft seal has leaked.
sections.job_setup_note: The green system must be depressurised at the reservoir and the accumulator discharged before any joint is broken. Fluid in the drive pad cavity must be measured and recorded before it is wiped away, because the quantity decides whether the pump is scrapped or returned for overhaul. Have the collection tray in position before the pump is withdrawn.
sections.procedure: 1. Open the fan cowl and get access to the pump from zone 123. 2. Depressurise the green system at the reservoir and discharge the accumulator. WARNING: THE GREEN SYSTEM ACCUMULATOR STORES ENERGY EVEN WITH THE ENGINE SHUT DOWN. CONFIRM ZERO PRESSURE AT THE GAUGE BEFORE YOU BREAK ANY JOINT. 3. Position the fluid collection tray beneath the pump. 4. Disconnect the electrical connector at the solenoid of FIN 16GG. 5. Release the clamp at FIN 280GG8 and move the case drain line clear. 6. Disconnect the suction and delivery lines and cap them immediately. 7. Remove the mounting nuts and withdraw the pump squarely from the drive pad. CAUTION: WITHDRAW THE PUMP SQUARELY. TILTING IT WILL DAMAGE THE SPLINE AND THE PAD SEAL. 8. Measure and record the quantity of fluid in the drive pad cavity before you wipe it. 9. Inspect the drive spline for wear and record the condition. 10. Where the valve D2910110251872 is being changed with the pump, remove it now. 11. Fit the blanking plate to the drive pad and cap the pump ports.
sections.close_out: Fit the blanking plate to the drive pad and cap all open ports. Record the pump serial number, the hours since installation, the measured cavity fluid quantity and the spline condition on the component removal card. Dispose of the collected fluid through the approved route. Make an entry in the technical log that the green system is open.

safety_precautions: Confirm zero pressure at the gauge before you break any joint.
Wear gloves and eye protection when you handle phosphate ester fluid.
Position the collection tray before the pump is withdrawn.

title: Removal of the Green System Engine Driven Pump

issue.reason: Both shaft seal assemblies are now named in the task and the shop level restriction on the kit assembly is stated.

abstract: Removal of the green system engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox drive pad, with the drive pad cavity inspection and the rule that neither shaft seal assembly is disturbed while the pump is on the aircraft.

sections.purpose: This task removes the green system engine driven pump from the accessory gearbox drive pad and records the condition of the drive pad cavity, which is the evidence used to decide whether the shaft seal has leaked.
sections.job_setup_note: The green system must be depressurised at the reservoir and the accumulator discharged before any joint is broken. Fluid in the drive pad cavity must be measured and recorded before it is wiped away, because the quantity decides whether the pump is scrapped or returned for overhaul. Have the collection tray in position before the pump is withdrawn. Two shaft seal assemblies are in service: the original assembly D2910110251872 and the interim kit assembly GRDE393470-41 introduced by MOD-151295. Neither is a line task. Whichever is fitted, the seal is changed in the shop with the pump off the aircraft, and this task ends at the removal.
sections.procedure: 1. Open the fan cowl and get access to the pump from zone 123. 2. Depressurise the green system at the reservoir and discharge the accumulator. WARNING: THE GREEN SYSTEM ACCUMULATOR STORES ENERGY EVEN WITH THE ENGINE SHUT DOWN. CONFIRM ZERO PRESSURE AT THE GAUGE BEFORE YOU BREAK ANY JOINT. 3. Position the fluid collection tray beneath the pump. 4. Disconnect the electrical connector at the solenoid of FIN 16GG. 5. Release the clamp at FIN 280GG8 and move the case drain line clear. 6. Disconnect the suction and delivery lines and cap them immediately. 7. Remove the mounting nuts and withdraw the pump squarely from the drive pad. CAUTION: WITHDRAW THE PUMP SQUARELY. TILTING IT WILL DAMAGE THE SPLINE AND THE PAD SEAL. 8. Measure and record the quantity of fluid in the drive pad cavity before you wipe it. 9. Inspect the drive spline for wear and record the condition. 10. Read the shaft seal standard from the pump data plate and record it: the original assembly D2910110251872 or the interim kit assembly GRDE393470-41. CAUTION: NEITHER SHAFT SEAL ASSEMBLY IS CHANGED ON THE AIRCRAFT. BOTH ARE SHOP LEVEL FITS. SEND THE PUMP TO THE SHOP. 11. Where the valve D2910110251872 is being changed with the pump, remove it now with the pump as one unit. 12. Fit the blanking plate to the drive pad and cap the pump ports.
sections.close_out: Fit the blanking plate to the drive pad and cap all open ports. Record the pump serial number, the hours since installation, the measured cavity fluid quantity and the spline condition on the component removal card. Dispose of the collected fluid through the approved route. Make an entry in the technical log that the green system is open.

type_data.effectivity_note: All classic model aircraft; both shaft seal assemblies are shop level fits and are not changed on the aircraft

safety_precautions: Confirm zero pressure at the gauge before you break any joint.
Wear gloves and eye protection when you handle phosphate ester fluid.
Position the collection tray before the pump is withdrawn.
Do not attempt a shaft seal change with the pump on the drive pad.
